Streets, schools and transit near Steveston North condos

items.t: Steveston North is the residential district in Richmond's south-west, north of the historic Steveston village and south of Blundell Road. "Steveston North" is the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® (GVR) board sub-area name; the City does not use it as a planning name — the district spans the northern part of the Steveston planning area (Steveston Area Plan, Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 9000) and edges into the City's Seafair planning area to the north.

No market figures are stated for this area: Richmond is not covered in the SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report, whose GVR communities are Burnaby, New Westminster, Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, Port Moody, Pitt Meadows and Maple Ridge only — no sub-area inventory, sales, sales ratio, median, $/sqft, sale-to-list or days-on-market figure exists in the permitted source for Steveston North, and none is substituted.

Anchors: Hugh Boyd Community Park, 9200 No. 1 Road (pitch and putt, artificial turf fields, tennis courts, playground), with West Richmond Community Centre on the same site; the West Dyke Trail runs along the western dike at the district's west edge.
Grauer Elementary, 4440 Blundell Rd; Alfred B. Dixon Elementary, 9331 Diamond Rd (north-west edge); John G. 1 Road. 1 Road.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 401 runs on No. 1 Road between Steveston Exchange and Richmond–Brighouse Station (Canada Line), stopping beside Hugh Boyd Park. Main roads: No. 1 Road north–south, Francis Road and Williams Road east–west, Blundell Road at the north edge, Steveston Highway at the south edge running east to Highway 99.

Flood frame: the district is on Lulu Island in the Fraser River floodplain, behind the City perimeter dike system with drainage pump stations, designed for a 1:500 flood event with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres; the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction level requirements.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it does not. The district's documented housing form is single-detached houses in the RS1/RS2 zones under Zoning Bylaw No. 8500, and the district's named new strata complexes are townhouses, not apartment condos.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Steveston North

items.t: Richmond property taxes: property taxes are due once a year on the first business day of July — Thursday, July 2, 2026 — with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after that date and a further 5% penalty on balances still outstanding after September 1, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston North condos

items.t: BC Housing groups Richmond differently from the real estate board. The Zone 3 directory's "Richmond — West" and "Richmond — South" groupings cut across the board's Steveston sub-areas — Ukrainian Village is a "Richmond — West" listing on a Steveston street — so a subsidized-housing search by board sub-area name will miss buildings a Steveston North senior can actually apply for.

The district's newest strata stock is townhouses, and both named complexes carry a void rental line. Heron (2022) and Innova30 (2023) record "rentals allowed with restrictions" — a restriction form that has been unenforceable for long-term rentals since November 24, 2022.

A provincial school investment lands at the district's north-west edge. The Province's February 2026 announcement lists seismic upgrades at Alfred B. Dixon Elementary (9331 Diamond Road) among Richmond projects opening in 2026.

The recreation anchor is a combined park, school and community centre site. Hugh Boyd Community Park, Hugh Boyd Secondary School and West Richmond Community Centre share the 9200 No. 1 Road site, with the route 401 bus stopping beside it.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Steveston South
Imperial Landing — 12333 English Avenue (directory address), Bayview Street at the south end of No. 1 Road

Onni's waterfront development on the former BC Packers cannery site, including The Village at Imperial Landing, per the developer's brochure; current listings place units at 4111 Bayview Street in Imperial Landing in the Steveston South sub-area. The building directory records the 12333 English Avenue building as built 2004 with 45 units, a club house, and published restrictions: pets allowed, rentals allowed.
The Village — 4280 Moncton Street / 4211 Bayview Street

A strata complex built 2005, per the building directory and current MLS listings, which record sub-type Apartment/Condo, freehold strata title, frame-wood construction and 4 storeys for units at 4280 Moncton Street in the Steveston South sub-area. Published restrictions according to the strata directory: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. A published age restriction: none appears — listing copy markets units to downsizers, but a downsizer marketing line is not a 55+ bylaw.
Streets, schools and transit near Steveston South condos

items.t: Steveston South is the south-west corner of the City of Richmond, on the South Arm of the Fraser River. "Steveston South" is the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® (GVR) board sub-area name; the City does not use it as a planning name — the district sits inside the Steveston planning area governed by the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 9000).

Anchors: Garry Point Park, a 39-acre waterfront park at the mouth of the Fraser River; Imperial Landing Waterfront Park on the historic BC Packers cannery site; the West Dyke Trail; Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, a 30-acre park with the Steveston Community Centre, pool and library complex; Richmond Public Library's Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub) at 4320 Moncton Street; the Gulf of Georgia Cannery at 12138 4th Avenue, a national historic site.
McMath Secondary, 4251 Garry St. SD38 catchments are address-based with no middle school tier; confirm the catchment for an exact address in the SD38 School Locator before relying on it.

Transit and roads: buses serve Steveston Exchange on Chatham Street, including TransLink route 401 to Richmond–Brighouse Station via No. 1 Road for Canada Line connections. Main roads: Moncton Street through the village, No. 1 Road north to Richmond centre, Steveston Highway east to Highway 99, Railway Avenue north–south at the east side, and No. 2 Road north from the village.

Flood frame: the district fronts the South Arm of the Fraser River behind the City dike system — Richmond is a low-lying island city in the Fraser River floodplain protected by a perimeter dike system with drainage pump stations, designed for a 1:500 flood event with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres — and the City's Steveston Island Dike project addresses the Steveston waterfront and harbour; Bylaw No. 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction level requirements.
The balance of the district is single-detached houses under Zoning Bylaw No. 8500 RS1/RS2 zones, with secondary suites permitted under Section 5.4.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Steveston South

items.t: Heritage: the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area sits at the district's south-west waterfront; properties inside it are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston South condos

items.t: Two "Landings" and a "Village" share these streets, and none of the names mean what a search assumes. Contracts and strata documents run under the specific building name and address.

Garry Street is a seniors-housing street because of a temple land deal. Wisteria Place exists because the Steveston Buddhist Temple retained ownership of its land and spearheaded the project through a separate non-profit, the Wisteria Senior Health and Housing Society, with Optima Living as operator — which is why Steveston South's newest seniors building is non-profit rental beside the temple, not a strata project a buyer can purchase into. Lions Park and River's End Co-op sit on the same street.

Imperial Landing's own dates do not agree with each other. The building directory gives 2004 and 45 units for the English Avenue building; the 2011 Richmond Review history records building permits approved that year for six waterfront buildings with 52 homes expected on the same Bayview lands. A buyer comparing "Imperial Landing" units across phases is comparing different buildings and vintages under one name.

The flood project has a navigation gate in it. The City's Steveston Island Dike project proposes a dike around Steveston Island from London Farm to Garry Point Park with a navigation gate for Steveston Harbour — flood protection here has to keep a working fishing harbour open.

Minato West's two official descriptions describe two different buildings. BC Housing's seniors directory lists it as seniors housing; its operator, Metro Vancouver, describes a general affordable complex of 110 suites built in 1977. Verify the current tenancy mix with the operator before treating it as seniors housing.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Steveston Village
Streets, schools and transit near Steveston Village condos

items.t: Steveston Village is the historic village core within the Steveston planning area of the City of Richmond, governed by the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 9000). The City designates the core as the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area in the Steveston Area Plan. "Steveston Village" is also the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® (GVR) board sub-area name for the core.

Rough extent of the core: along Moncton Street and Chatham Street between No. 1 Road to the east and 7th Avenue and the waterfront to the west, with the South Arm of the Fraser River and Dyke Road to the south and Steveston Highway to the north. Properties inside the heritage conservation area are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan.

Anchors: the Gulf of Georgia Cannery at 12138 4th Avenue, a national historic site; Garry Point Park, a 39-acre waterfront park at the mouth of the Fraser River; Imperial Landing Waterfront Park on the historic BC Packers cannery site; Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, a 30-acre park with the Steveston Community Centre, pool and library complex; Richmond Public Library's Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub) at 4320 Moncton Street. Shops, markets and services centre on Moncton Street, and the harbour has a public fish sales float.

Schools: public schools in the Steveston area beside the village core include Westwind Elementary School, 11371 Kingfisher Drive, and R.A. McMath Secondary School, 4251 Garry Street — both Ministry-listed names.

Flood frame: the village sits on the South Arm of the Fraser River behind the City dike system (perimeter dikes with drainage pump stations, designed for a 1:500 event, dike raising from 3.5 m to 4.7 m under way), and the City's Steveston Island Dike project addresses flood protection for the Steveston waterfront and harbour; Bylaw No. 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction level requirements.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it does not, as apartment condos. The core's housing is detached houses on side streets plus low-rise mixed-use strata over Moncton/Chatham Street retail under Commercial Mixed Use (ZMU32) – Steveston Village and Steveston Commercial (CS3) zoning, and the one strata building named for the village is townhouse-form with a retail unit.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Steveston Village

items.t: Heritage — the defining rule of this sub-area: Steveston Village is designated as a heritage conservation area in the Steveston Area Plan; protected heritage buildings and other resource types such as docks and landscape features are identified in the Official Community Plan, and properties inside the conservation area are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements. A buyer of a village house or mixed-use strata unit is buying into alteration controls other Richmond neighbourhoods do not carry.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston Village condos

items.t: The village's biggest seniors building exists because a veterans' branch gave up its land. The Maple Residences project was developed by the Steveston 284 Seniors' Housing Society — formed by the Army, Navy and Air Force Veterans of Canada (Unit 284) with Steveston (Unit 284) Holdings Ltd. — on the ANAF site at No. 1 Road and Chatham Street, as 144 seniors' units plus a commercial building containing the ANAF lounge and clubhouse. That is why the core's seniors housing is non-profit rental beside a veterans' clubhouse, not a strata building.

Two seniors buildings share one Chatham Street block, with two different admission doors. The Maple Residences (serviced rental, apply to the society) and Bill Rigby Senior Apartments (subsidized, apply through BC Housing's Housing Registry) stand at 4071 and 4100 Chatham Street — a buyer touring one will see the other, and they are not the same product, price system or application route.

Heritage protection here covers more than houses. The Steveston Area Plan's conservation area identifies protected heritage buildings and other resource types such as docks and landscape features in the Official Community Plan — a waterfront village lot can carry protected features that are not a building at all.

items.t: Where the housing stock concentrates: overwhelmingly single-detached houses in the RS1/RS2 zones — the district's documented form on official sources.

Parks and recreation: Hugh Boyd Community Park, 9200 No. 1 Road, has a pitch and putt course, artificial turf fields, turf sports fields, basketball courts, tennis courts, a playground and paved walking paths; West Richmond Community Centre sits at the park, with a fitness centre, gymnasium, squash court and badminton courts. The West Dyke Trail runs along the western dike at the district's west edge.

Main roads: No. 1 Road north–south through the district, Francis Road and Williams Road east–west, Blundell Road at the north edge, Steveston Highway at the south edge running east to Highway 99. Transit: TransLink route 401 runs on No. 1 Road between Steveston Exchange and Richmond–Brighouse Station (Canada Line), stopping beside Hugh Boyd Park and Hugh Boyd Secondary School.

Schools physically in or beside the district: Hugh Boyd Secondary School, 9200 No. 1 Road; R.M. Grauer Elementary, 4440 Blundell Road; Alfred B. Dixon Elementary, 9331 Diamond Road, at the district's north-west edge (seismic upgrades at Dixon were among the Richmond projects the Province announced in February 2026 as opening in 2026). School District 38 catchments are address-based and the district has no middle-school tier. School names here are Ministry-listed names only.
Nearby areas: Steveston South and Steveston Village (south), Seafair and Boyd Park / West Richmond (north), London/Steveston (east).
Library and hospital: nearest full-service library is Richmond Public Library's Brighouse (Main) Branch, 100-7700 Minoru Gate; nearest hospital is Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston North townhomes

items.t: Heron's unit count depends on which secondary source you open. The listing panel and the developer record say 28 homes; the building directory's headline says a 22-unit development. The Form B and strata plan settle it — until then, any per-unit fee or CRF comparison built on either number is provisional.

The north/south line runs through the counted complex's front yard. Heron fronts Steveston Highway, the listing-practice split between Steveston North and Steveston South — a search filtered to "Steveston South" can hide the district's only counted townhouse complex, and vice versa.

For 9200 No. 1 Road — Hugh Boyd Community Park and Hugh Boyd Secondary School's own address — the SD38 locator gives Diefenbaker Elementary and Boyd Secondary: the secondary school on the site is the catchment school, but the elementary catchment is a different school than a buyer standing in the park would assume, and every other address needs its own run.

A Dixon Elementary seismic upgrade lands in 2026. The Province's February 2026 announcement lists seismic upgrades at Alfred B. Dixon Elementary (9331 Diamond Road, the district's north-west edge) among Richmond projects opening in 2026 — a dated, official investment fact for the district's north end.
One No. 1 Road complex is claimed by three geographies and counted by none.

London Landing townhouses — 13200 Princess Street.

City of Richmond council material from 2002 documents a townhouse development by London Landing Development Corp. The neighbouring Princess Lane / Currents entries above are separate, later strata product and are not assumed to be this development.
Streets, schools and transit near Steveston South townhomes

items.t: Parks and waterfront: Garry Point Park, a 39-acre waterfront park at the mouth of the Fraser River; Imperial Landing Waterfront Park on the historic BC Packers cannery site; the West Dyke Trail along the west dike; the Steveston Greenways linking the waterfront and historic sites; Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, a 30-acre park with the Steveston Community Centre, pool and library complex; Richmond Public Library's Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub) at 4320 Moncton Street. The Gulf of Georgia Cannery at 12138 4th Avenue is a national historic site. The Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area sits at the district's south-west waterfront, and properties inside it are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan.

Main roads: Moncton Street through the village, No. 1 Road north to Richmond centre, Steveston Highway east to Highway 99, Railway Avenue north–south at the east side of Steveston, and No. 2 Road north from the village. Transit: buses serve Steveston Exchange on Chatham Street, including TransLink route 401 (One Road) to Richmond–Brighouse Station via No. 1 Road for Canada Line connections.

Schools physically in the district: Lord Byng Elementary School, 3711 Georgia Street; Steves Elementary School, 10111 Fourth Avenue; Westwind Elementary School, 11371 Kingfisher Drive; R.A. McMath Secondary School, 4251 Garry Street, one of Richmond's two French Immersion secondary schools.

Nearby areas: Steveston Village (the historic core, inside this district's south-west), Steveston North (across Steveston Highway), London/Steveston and South Arm (to the east), Seafair (to the north-east).

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston South townhomes

items.t: The district holds real townhouses that no buyer can buy. Minato West's 80 townhouses (Metro Vancouver's count, inside its 110-suite affordable complex, built 1977) are the largest townhouse-form cluster in the district after London Landing — and they are non-profit rental, invisible to every "townhouses for sale" search for a tenure reason, not a form reason.

The fishing pier name is a family, not a direction. In 1881 brothers Charles and William London bought 200 acres at the south end of No. 2 Road at what became known as London's Landing — every official use since (the ZMU zones, the wharf park, the buildings) descends from that family name, which is why "Lower Landing" finds nothing in any City source.
Two London Stations, two forms. 6111 London Road is the counted townhouse-form complex (built 2007); 6077 London Road — London Station II — is apartment-form stock (built 2009).

The district's civic anchor sits inside its park. Steveston Community Park (4011 Moncton Street, 30 acres) holds the Steveston Community Centre, pool and library complex, and the Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub) library is at 4320 Moncton Street — village-edge townhouse buyers use these facilities, not in-pocket ones.

The waterfront the condos front was a cannery. Imperial Landing Waterfront Park sits on the historic BC Packers cannery site (the development is 6.5 acres of waterfront on that site per the City's Greenways material) — the heritage-industrial history is the setting for the Bayview Street strata stock, and the Britannia Shipyards National Heritage Site sits west along the same Greenways.

Streets, schools and transit near Steveston Village townhomes

items.t: Where the housing stock concentrates: detached houses on the village side streets (RS1/RS2 zones), with the core itself mixed use — City reports name Commercial Mixed Use (ZMU32) – Steveston Village on Chatham Street and Steveston Commercial (CS3) zoning in the core, so the strata housing in the core is in low-rise mixed-use buildings over Moncton/Chatham Street retail.

Village anchors: the Gulf of Georgia Cannery at 12138 4th Avenue, a national historic site associated with the West Coast fishing industry; Garry Point Park, a 39-acre waterfront park at the mouth of the Fraser River close to the village; Imperial Landing Waterfront Park on the historic BC Packers cannery site; the West Dyke Trail and the Steveston Greenways linking the waterfront and historic sites; Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, a 30-acre park with the Steveston Community Centre, pool and library in the park complex; Richmond Public Library's Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub) at 4320 Moncton Street. Shops, markets and services centre on Moncton Street, and the harbour has a public fish sales float.

Main roads: Moncton Street through the village core, No. 1 Road north to Richmond centre, Steveston Highway east to Highway 99, Railway Avenue north–south at the east side of the village, and No. 2 Road north from the village.
Nearby areas: Steveston South and Steveston North (the surrounding residential districts), London/Steveston to the east, Seafair to the north-east.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Steveston Village

items.t: Heritage overlay — the village-specific rule: properties inside the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of OCP Bylaw 9000), and the conservation area identifies protected heritage buildings and other resource types such as docks and landscape features — a waterfront village lot can carry protected features that are not a building at all. The building sits between Chatham and Moncton Streets in the historic core; confirm the permit position before pricing in any exterior work.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston Village townhomes

items.t: The village was a working cannery town, and the cannery is a national historic site. The Gulf of Georgia Cannery at 12138 4th Avenue is a national historic site associated with the West Coast fishing industry; the village was once a centre of salmon fishing and canning, and First Nations peoples harvested the land and waters of the region for thousands of years before settlement.

The core's flood project has a navigation gate in it. The City's Steveston Island Dike project proposes a dike around Steveston Island from London Farm to Garry Point Park with a navigation gate for Steveston Harbour — flood protection here has to keep a working harbour working, which is why it is a named, staged project rather than a simple dike raise.

The village's strata stock hides inside its retail streets. The core is zoned for low-rise mixed use over Moncton/Chatham retail (ZMU32, CS3) — a buyer searching only residential streets will miss the form entirely, and the one named townhouse-form building carries a retail unit inside the same strata.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Steveston North
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Lot character and minimums: houses sit in Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500 Single Detached zones RS1 and RS2 (Section 8.1), with minimum lot areas by subzone including RS1/B 360.0 m², RS1/E 550.0 m², RS1/F 828.0 m² and RS1/K 315.0 m², and a 24.0 m minimum depth in most subzones. A secondary suite is a permitted secondary use in the RS1/RS2 zones, and Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing zones (RSM/S, RSM/M, RSM/L, RSM/XL) are applied under Bill 44. The subzone of a specific lot can be confirmed in Bylaw 8500 Section 8.1.8.
Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Steveston North is confirmed and no split is stated — ALR status is a per-parcel check on ALC mapping.

Flood position: the district is on Lulu Island in the Fraser River floodplain, behind the City perimeter dike system with drainage pump stations; the system is designed for a 1:500 flood event and dikes are being raised from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres for sea level rise. The Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction level requirements — confirm the lot's flood construction level with the City before pricing a rebuild.

blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: Heron was developer-marketed as a presale project before its Spring 2022 completion; it is completed stock today and is not a presale lot offering.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Steveston North lots

items.t: Steveston North is the City of Richmond's residential district in the city's south-west, north of the historic Steveston village and south of Blundell Road. The board sub-area name is "Steveston North" (GVR listing data); the City does not use "Steveston North" as a planning name — the district spans the northern part of the Steveston planning area (Steveston Area Plan, Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan) and edges into the City's Seafair planning area to the north. Nearby areas: Steveston South and Steveston Village (south), Seafair and Boyd Park / West Richmond (north), London/Steveston (east).

Parks and recreation: Hugh Boyd Community Park (9200 No. 1 Road) has a pitch and putt course, artificial turf fields, turf sports fields, basketball courts, tennis courts, a playground and paved walking paths, with West Richmond Community Centre on site (fitness centre, gymnasium, squash court, badminton courts); the West Dyke Trail runs along the western dike at the district's west edge.
Transit: TransLink route 401 runs on No. 1 Road between Steveston Exchange and Richmond–Brighouse Station (Canada Line), stopping beside Hugh Boyd Park and Hugh Boyd Secondary School.
Nearest hospital: Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway. Nearest full-service library: Richmond Public Library Brighouse (Main) Branch, 100-7700 Minoru Gate.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Steveston North

items.t: Planning framework — Richmond 2041 OCP, Bylaw 9000 + Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4): the district spans the northern part of the Steveston planning area governed by the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the OCP), edging into the Seafair planning area to the north. Confirm which plan area a specific lot sits in before relying on plan policy.

Zoning — Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500, RS1/RS2 (Section 8.1): minimum lot areas by subzone (RS1/B 360.0 m²; RS1/E 550.0 m²; RS1/F 828.0 m²; RS1/K 315.0 m²; 24.0 m minimum depth in most subzones); a secondary suite is a permitted secondary use.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Steveston South
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Lot character and minimums: houses sit in Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500 Single Detached zones RS1 and RS2 (Section 8.1), with minimum lot sizes varying by subzone in Section 8.1.8 — for example RS1/B 360.0 m², RS1/E 550.0 m², RS1/F 828.0 m² and RS1/K 315.0 m², with a 24.0 m minimum depth in most subzones.

Suite rules on the lot, as the bylaw states them: a secondary suite in a single-detached house must meet Section 5.4 of Bylaw 8500 — at least 33.0 m², and at most the lesser of 40% of the dwelling floor area or 110 m².
Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Steveston South is confirmed and no split is stated — ALR status is a per-parcel check on ALC mapping.

Flood and heritage overlays on the lots themselves: the district fronts the South Arm of the Fraser River behind the City dike system (1:500 design; dikes being raised from 3.5 m to 4.7 m; the City's Steveston Island Dike project addresses the Steveston waterfront and harbour), and Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels. At the south-west waterfront, lots inside the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area need a Heritage Alteration Permit for exterior changes — an overlay that affects renovation and rebuild plans lot by lot.

blocks.text: Built developments on former industrial / assembly ground

items.t: Imperial Landing — Bayview Street at the south end of No. 1 Road.: It is the district's documented example of cannery land redeveloped as built strata — the land story is closed; no lot in it is bare-land inventory.
London Landing ground — the district's east edge (official name: London Landing)
The Steveston Village building (12040 2nd Avenue) and McKinney Walk belong primarily to the steveston-village ground.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Steveston South lots

items.t: Steveston South is the City of Richmond's south-west corner, on the South Arm of the Fraser River. The board sub-area name is "Steveston South" (GVR listing data); the City does not use "Steveston South" as a planning name — the district sits inside the Steveston planning area governed by the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the City Official Community Plan). Nearby areas: Steveston Village (the historic core, inside this district's south-west), Steveston North (across Steveston Highway), London/Steveston and South Arm (to the east), Seafair (to the north-east).

The Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area sits at the district's south-west waterfront, and properties inside it are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan.

Schools physically in the district: Lord Byng Elementary School (3711 Georgia Street); Steves Elementary School (10111 Fourth Avenue); Westwind Elementary School (11371 Kingfisher Drive); R.A. McMath Secondary School (4251 Garry Street), one of Richmond's two French Immersion secondary schools.
Shopping: village shops, markets and services are centred on Moncton Street, with a public fish sales float at the harbour.
Nearest hospital: Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Steveston South

items.t: Heritage — Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area: properties inside the conservation area at the district's south-west waterfront are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan; near the village, check heritage status first — it affects renovation plans and timelines on the lot.

Zoning — Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500, RS1/RS2 (Section 8.1) + suite rules: minimum lot sizes by subzone in Section 8.1.8 (RS1/B 360.0 m²; RS1/E 550.0 m²; RS1/F 828.0 m²; RS1/K 315.0 m²; 24.0 m minimum depth in most subzones); secondary suites under Section 5.4 (minimum 33.0 m²; maximum the lesser of 40% of the dwelling or 110 m²). Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing zones RSM/S, RSM/M, RSM/L and RSM/XL were added under provincial Bill 44 legislation.

Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204 + Steveston Island Dike: the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels; for waterfront and dyke-adjacent lots, confirm both before pricing in a rebuild or addition, and watch the City's Steveston Island Dike project — its named long-term flood project for this waterfront.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston South lots

items.t: The waterfront strata sits on a cannery site, and a similarly named property is not it: Imperial Landing stands on the historic BC Packers cannery site at the south end of No. 1 Road, while Steveston Landing (3800 Bayview Street) is a five-storey mixed-use commercial/retail property built 1989 on the same street — same street, different properties, and only the first is residential strata.

The flood project has a name a buyer can follow: the Steveston Island Dike project is the City's named long-term flood project for this waterfront — a Steveston South lot's flood position is tracked through that project and Bylaw 8204, not through generic Richmond floodplain copy.

The fish float is a working-harbour detail, not a marketing line: village services centre on Moncton Street with a public fish sales float at the harbour, and the Gulf of Georgia Cannery (12138 4th Avenue) is a national historic site — the village-core lots sit inside a working fishing harbour's heritage fabric, which is exactly why the Heritage Conservation Area permit regime exists there.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Steveston Village lots

items.t: Steveston Village is the historic village core inside the wider Steveston planning area in the City of Richmond, BC, governed by the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the City Official Community Plan); the City designates the core as the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area in that plan. "Steveston Village" is also the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® (GVR) board sub-area name for the core.
Transit: buses serve Steveston Exchange on Chatham Street, including TransLink route 401 One Road to Richmond–Brighouse Station via No. 1 Road, for Canada Line connections.

Landmarks that frame the land: the Gulf of Georgia Cannery at 12138 4th Avenue is a national historic site; Garry Point Park is a 39-acre waterfront park at the mouth of the Fraser River; Imperial Landing Waterfront Park sits on the historic BC Packers cannery site; Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, is a 30-acre park with the community centre, pool and library.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Steveston Village

items.t: Plan — Steveston Area Plan within OCP Bylaw 9000: the current plan is the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan), within the City of Richmond 2041 Official Community Plan framework, Bylaw 9000.
Zoning — Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500: Confirm the parcel's zone with the City before pricing any rebuild, addition or split.

Heritage Alteration Permits: properties inside the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan — check heritage status before anything else, because it affects renovation plans, timelines and resale positioning.

Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204: the village sits on the South Arm of the Fraser River behind the City dike system — Richmond is a low-lying city in the Fraser River floodplain protected by a perimeter dike system (49 km of dikes, 39 pump stations, designed for a 1:500 flood event, dikes being raised from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres) with drainage pump stations; the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction level requirements. The City's Steveston Island Dike project — a proposed dike around Steveston Island from London Farm to Garry Point Park with a navigation gate for Steveston Harbour — addresses flood protection for the Steveston waterfront and harbour. Verify the lot's flood construction level and dike setback before planning a rebuild.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steveston Village lots

items.t: The village's name is also a building's name — and the building is not part of this count: the strata building at 12040 2nd Avenue is called "Steveston Village," which invites double-counting against the neighbourhood itself.

The dike is being re-thought around the village itself: the Steveston Island Dike project proposes a dike around Steveston Island from London Farm to Garry Point Park with a navigation gate for Steveston Harbour — flood diligence here is a live City project, not a settled historic fact.

faq.a: Both are townhouse strata — Heron (5651 Steveston Highway, 2022, 28 units per listing data) and Innova30 (7580 No. 1 Road, 2023, 30 homes).
faq.q: Is Heron or Innova30 a condo?

faq.a: Long-term, yes as a matter of provincial law — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022, whatever the recorded "rentals allowed with restrictions" line says. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw; read the registered bylaws on the Form B package.
faq.q: Can I rent out a unit at Heron or Innova30?

faq.a: No — Ukrainian Village (8720 Railway Avenue) is non-profit subsidized seniors rental in BC Housing's Zone 3 directory, applied for through the Housing Registry; Maple Vine Court (7500 Francis Road) is likewise non-profit rental and also appears in BC Housing's family directory. Neither is strata ownership.
faq.q: Is Ukrainian Village a condo I can buy?

faq.a: SD38 catchments are address-based, with no middle-school tier. 1 Road; Hugh Boyd Secondary is at 9200 No. 1 Road itself and R.M. Grauer Elementary is at 4440 Blundell Road. Run the exact address in the locator before relying on any school.
faq.q: Which schools serve a Steveston North address?

faq.a: On the waterfront strip and the village edge: Imperial Landing (12333 English Avenue directory address; units also at 4111 Bayview Street) and The Village (4280 Moncton Street / 4211 Bayview Street, built 2005).
faq.q: Where are the condos in Steveston South, actually?

faq.a: Several. The developer history records six waterfront buildings on the Bayview Street lands with about 60,000 square feet of residential space over commercial space, and the directory carries the name at 12333 English Avenue (built 2004, 45 units) while current listings place Imperial Landing units at 4111 Bayview Street — establish which building and strata plan a specific unit sits in before comparing across the name.
faq.q: Is Imperial Landing one building or several?

faq.a: No — both are rental. Wisteria Place (4388 Garry Street) is a 107-suite rental independent-living residence operated by Optima Living on land retained by the Steveston Buddhist Temple; Lions Park (4200–4206 Garry Street) is BC Housing subsidized seniors rental through the Housing Registry; Steveston Residence is non-profit supportive rental, and Garry Point, River's End and Richmond Project are co-ops — none is strata ownership.
faq.q: Are Wisteria Place or Lions Park condos I can buy?

faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. Check the title first.
faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex in Steveston South?

faq.a: Steveston is the district name; the board listing names are Steveston North, Steveston South and Steveston Village, while the City plans the area under the Steveston Area Plan, Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan, and designates the core as the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area.
faq.q: Is Steveston a City of Richmond neighbourhood name?

faq.a: Confirmed against the BC Ministry K-12 file: Lord Byng Elementary (3711 Georgia St), Westwind Elementary (11371 Kingfisher Dr) and Diefenbaker Elementary (4511 Hermitage Dr), with R.A. McMath Secondary (4251 Garry St) and Hugh Boyd Secondary (9200 No. 1 Rd) serving the district's sides; catchments are address-based, so confirm the exact address in the SD38 locator.
